title: Former Kinsmen centre redevelopment and police surplus motion
subtitle: Also: future of 134 Frederick Street, development charge indexing, and a deferred notice of motion on police surpluses.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that staff explore turning the Region-owned former Kinsmen Children's Centre at 651 Concession Road, Cambridge, into a multi-use building. Possible uses include Paramedic Services, affordable housing and other integrated social services. Staff were also directed to apply for a Federation of Canadian Municipalities study grant. The committee's recommendation goes to Council for adoption, and staff expect to return in 2024 with a detailed proposal and updated cost estimate {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also deferred a notice of motion on how future police surpluses are shared between the Waterloo Region Police Service reserves and the Region. It was deferred to November 7, 2023 so staff can prepare a report and legal opinion, and the police service can comment {{vote:m6}}.

The committee heard an information report on 134 Frederick Street, Kitchener, which is being vacated by police. Staff said recommendations on its future use are expected in late 2024 or early 2025. Staff will also report back on possible locations for an Indigenous hub. The consent agenda, which included development charge indexing and a quarterly tenders summary, was received for information {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Former Kinsmen Children's Centre, 651 Concession Road
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff explore redeveloping the site as a Regional multi-use building with Paramedic Services, affordable housing and possibly other social services, and apply for a Federation of Canadian Municipalities Sustainable Affordable Housing study grant.

decisions.item: Notice of motion on police surpluses
decisions.detail: The committee deferred the motion to split future surpluses between police reserves and the Region until November 7, 2023, pending a staff report, legal opinion and comment from Waterloo Region Police Service.
The committee received for information, and approved, the consent items, including the development charge indexing report and the quarterly summary of tenders and quotations.

debate: On the Cambridge site, councillors broadly supported the concept. One councillor asked that supportive housing be considered, and another supported affordable housing but opposed supportive housing there because the site is next to an elementary school.

Others replied that supportive housing is needed and that the committee should not rule out one type of housing before staff report back. Staff said the recommendation is general and the appendix rendering is only a possible concept.
On paramedic funding, staff said the province does not fund capital costs directly. It does cover 50% of the asset's amortization over the building's life.

On the police surplus motion, the mover said it concerns only surpluses, not the police budget itself, and that the police should keep the money they need. Councillors asked whether the Police Services Act permits it, and the Regional Solicitor said an outside opinion would likely be sought.

One councillor asked that the deferral also bring comment from the Region and the police service on the effects on reserves, and this was added. Another councillor urged respectful debate in the coming budget process.
